hot.pointer_line: On now: the trawlers back at the Keratsini auction since 1 October, palamida at its peak, pomegranates and quinces at the laiki, clocks back on 25 October, Ohi Day on 28 October, the Athens Marathon closing the roads on 8 November and the new oil in November.

items.name: The trawlers are back at Keratsini
items.teaser: The summer trawl closure ended on 30 September: since 1 October the deep-water fish are back at auction
items.story: From 1 June to 30 September the Greek bottom trawlers stay in port, and the Piraeus counters live on the small-boat catch: gavros, sardela, marides. On 1 October the closure lifts and the boats unload again at the Keratsini ichthyoskala, the country's largest fish auction, where the crates are sold before dawn and go on to the fishmongers and laiki markets of Attica. Barbouni, koutsomoures, fangri and sinagrida return to the ice in the Mikrolimano fish houses within days, and the auction stays at full output through the winter.
items.why: October and November give the port its widest choice of wild fish: this is the time to order a whole fish or provision the galley.
facts: Trawl season reopened 1 Oct 2026; closed again 1 Jun-30 Sep 2027
Ichthyoskala Keratsiniou, the central fish auction
Fish by the kilo, prices change daily
The auction is wholesale and works before first light: eat its catch at the canteen inside rather than trying to buy a crate

items.name: Palamida, at its October peak
items.teaser: The port's own saying: October is the time of palamida, fat enough now to cure as lakerda
items.story: Palamida, the Atlantic bonito, runs through the Aegean in late summer and reaches the Piraeus counters at its best in October, which the port sums up in one line: October is the time of palamida. It is an oily, dark-fleshed fish, grilled in thick steaks or salted and cured into lakerda, the pale pressed slices served with raw onion and ouzo. By November the run tails off and kalamari and soupia take over the autumn plates, so the next six weeks are the window for a fresh steak or a first lakerda.
items.why: Ask the fish house whether the palamida came in that morning, and order it grilled before it is gone for the year.
facts: Peak October; tailing off through November 2026
Fish counters and psarotavernes across Piraeus
By the kilo; ask the price before it is cut
For lakerda, ask a fishmonger which shop cures its own this season

items.name: The clocks go back, Sunday 25 October
items.teaser: Greece leaves summer time at 04:00 on Sunday 25 October, and port evenings close an hour earlier
items.story: On Sunday 25 October 2026 Greece returns to winter time: at 04:00 the clocks go back to 03:00. From then on the light goes an hour earlier by the clock, so the evening view from the Kastella hill and the last light over Salamis and the Saronic move into the late afternoon. The port itself does not stop: ferries and the Keratsini auction keep their own schedules, but a timetable printed before the change can mislead anyone checking it against an unchanged ship's clock.
items.why: After 25 October book a hilltop or waterside table an hour earlier than a summer habit would suggest.
facts: Phones change by themselves; ship's clocks, crew rotas and ferry bookings made in summer do not

items.name: Pomegranates, quinces and chestnuts
items.teaser: The laiki stalls turn to pomegranate, quince, walnuts, chestnuts and the first green olives
items.story: In October the Piraeus street markets change colour. The summer tomato and watermelon piles give way to pomegranates, quinces, walnuts, chestnuts and the first green olives, and the new must arrives with the grape harvest. In November come the first citrus, cauliflower and leeks, and wild horta returns to the tavernas once the rains start. The ouzeri table follows: chestnuts roasted on street braziers, quince baked with the meat dishes, and pomegranate seeds over the salads.
items.why: Provision the galley at a laiki for fruit that travels well: quinces and pomegranates keep for weeks.
facts: Go early in the morning, before the best stalls thin out

items.name: Agourelaio, the new oil
items.teaser: November brings the olive harvest and the first green, peppery oil to the Piraeus tables
items.story: The olive harvest begins across Greece in November, and with it comes agourelaio, the first oil of the season, pressed from olives picked early and still green. It is cloudy, grassy and sharp at the back of the throat, poured over bread, beans and grilled fish in the weeks after pressing. In Piraeus there is no civic festival to mark it; the new oil simply turns up on the taverna tables and in the shops during November.
items.why: Ask a taverna whether the new oil is in, and taste it on plain bread before anything else.
facts: From November 2026, as the first pressings arrive
Buy in a dark tin, not clear plastic, if it is going to a galley

items.name: Ohi Day, Wednesday 28 October
items.teaser: A national holiday: a doxology at the Holy Trinity Cathedral and school parades across the city
items.story: On 28 October Greece marks the day in 1940 when it refused the Italian ultimatum, the Ohi, the No. It is a public holiday. In Piraeus the morning begins with a doxology at the Cathedral of Agia Triada, attended by the city's civil and military authorities, and schoolchildren march in the neighbourhood parades with flags. In 2020 the city dressed the Municipal Theatre's facade in the blue and white of the flag with projection mapping. In 2026 the day falls on a Wednesday.
items.why: Expect banks and many shops closed and central streets shut for the parades during the morning.
facts: Cathedral of Agia Triada and the city centre
2026 parade times and routes were not yet published on 14 Oct: check the Municipality of Piraeus the week before

items.name: The Authentic Marathon, Sunday 8 November
items.teaser: The race from Marathon to Athens closes central roads on Sunday 8 November: plan port transfers around it
items.story: The Athens Authentic Marathon runs on Sunday 8 November 2026 along the classic route from the town of Marathon to the Panathenaic Stadium in central Athens, with the start at about 08:30 and shorter races on Saturday 7 November. The course does not come to Piraeus, but the closures across central Athens and on the approach roads last much of the day, and taxis and transfers between the port and the city slow down with them.
items.why: On race morning use the metro or tram between Piraeus and the centre rather than a car.
facts: Sun 8 Nov 2026, start about 08:30; shorter races Sat 7 Nov
Marathon to the Panathenaic Stadium, Athens
Guests flying in that weekend should allow extra time from the airport to the berth

items.name: Agios Spyridon, 12 December
items.teaser: The patron saint of Piraeus is honoured on 12 December at his church on the Central Harbour quay
items.story: Saint Spyridon, a fourth-century bishop of Trimythous in Cyprus, is the patron of Piraeus, and his church stands on the waterfront of the Central Harbour. On 12 December the Metropolis of Piraeus holds an archpastoral liturgy there, after vespers the evening before, and in many years the saint's icon is carried through the streets in procession with clergy, the faithful and the city's officials. It is the local high point of the winter, a working day for the port but a feast for the city around it.
items.why: Walk to the quay in the morning to hear the bells and see the crowds at the church door.
facts: Church of Agios Spyridon, Central Harbour
Procession plans change year to year: check the Metropolis of Piraeus announcement

items.name: The Epiphany dive, 6 January
items.teaser: The cross is thrown into the winter harbour opposite Agios Spyridon, and young men dive for it
items.story: On 6 January, Theophania, the Metropolitan of Piraeus celebrates the liturgy at the Holy Trinity Cathedral and then leads the procession down to the pier opposite the church of Agios Spyridon. There the waters are blessed and a wooden cross is thrown into the harbour; a few dozen young men, and in some years divers of the Navy's underwater demolition unit, plunge into the cold sea to bring it back. In January 2026 thousands gathered on the quay for it.
items.why: Arrive well before the cross is thrown: the quay fills and the view is from the front rows only.
facts: The pier opposite Agios Spyridon, Central Harbour
Warm layers; the wind off the harbour is the coldest part of the morning

items.name: Dekapentavgoustos, 15 August
items.teaser: The Dormition empties the city and jams the ferry gates; the Saronic islands hold their village feasts
items.story: 15 August, the Dormition of the Virgin, is the peak of the Greek summer holiday. Athenians and Piraiots leave for their home islands and villages in the days before, so the Piraeus ferry gates are at their most crowded of the year while the city behind them goes quiet. Across the Saronic the islands hold their panigyria, the village feasts with music and food. Many family tavernas and suppliers close for part of August.
items.why: Avoid ferry departures on the days around the 15th unless the tickets are already in hand.
facts: Nationwide; the Piraeus ferry gates; village feasts on the Saronic islands
Ring a venue the week before: an August closure rarely shows on its website

items.name: Tsiknopempti and Clean Monday, 2027
items.teaser: The grills are lit on Thursday 4 March 2027; Lent begins on Clean Monday, 15 March
items.story: The Orthodox calendar counts back from Easter. With Easter on 2 May 2027, Clean Monday, Kathara Deftera, the first day of Lent and a public holiday, falls on Monday 15 March, and Tsiknopempti, Smoky Thursday, eleven days before, on 4 March. In 2026 the Municipality of Piraeus held its free Tsiknopempti party in the Tinaneios Garden on 12 February, with a band, the municipal wind orchestra, grilled meat and wine. On Clean Monday the meat stops and the ouzeris turn to octopus, taramosalata and lagana.
items.why: Book a grill table for Tsiknopempti night; on Clean Monday order the Lenten seafood meze.
facts: Tsiknopempti Thu 4 Mar 2027; Clean Monday Mon 15 Mar 2027
Buy lagana from a bakery the Sunday before Clean Monday

items.name: Orthodox Easter, 2 May 2027
items.teaser: Good Friday 30 April, the midnight Resurrection, then lamb on Sunday 2 May
items.story: Orthodox Easter 2027 falls on Sunday 2 May. On Good Friday, 30 April, every Piraeus parish carries its flower-covered epitaphios through the streets after dark. Near midnight on Saturday the churches go dark, the flame is passed hand to hand, and at Christos anesti the bells and fireworks go off over the harbour; families then go home to magiritsa. Sunday is lamb, kokoretsi and red eggs, and Monday 3 May is a holiday too. The port half-empties for the long weekend.
items.why: Provision by Thursday: many shops and suppliers close from Good Friday to Easter Monday.
facts: Good Friday 30 Apr; Easter Sunday 2 May; Easter Monday 3 May 2027
Tavernas that stay open fill for the Sunday lamb: book a week ahead

items.name: Days of the Sea and the Posidonia Cup
items.teaser: Two weeks of free events on the Piraeus waterfront, from late May to mid-June
items.story: Days of the Sea, Imeres Thalassas, is the Municipality of Piraeus's own festival of the sea. Its twelfth edition ran from 29 May to 14 June 2026, with more than 120 free events: a concert by Eleni Tsaligopoulou at Pasalimani to open, beach clean-ups at Freattyda, and the 5 km Posidonia Running Event from the Municipal Theatre. The Posidonia Cup sailing race, its twelfth edition, was sailed in the waters off Piraeus on Friday 29 May 2026. 2027 dates had not been announced by mid-October.
items.why: Come for an evening concert on the waterfront: the events are free and the port is at its liveliest.
facts: Late May to mid-June; 2026 ran 29 May-14 Jun; 2027 dates not yet announced
Pasalimani, Freattyda and the Piraeus waterfront
The full programme is published by the Municipality of Piraeus in May

items.name: Posidonia, the shipping week
items.teaser: Every second June the shipping world fills Piraeus for Posidonia; the next edition is in 2028
items.story: Posidonia, the international shipping exhibition held every two years since 1969, ran from 1 to 5 June 2026 at the Metropolitan Expo near the airport, with a record 24 national pavilions. Its effect reaches the port: in Posidonia week shipowners, brokers and their guests book out the Mikrolimano and Zea tables and the yacht basins, and receptions run every night. It is held in even years, so the next edition is in 2028; its dates had not been announced by mid-October 2026.
items.why: In a Posidonia year book Mikrolimano dinners weeks ahead, not days.
facts: Early June in even years; 2026 ran 1-5 Jun; 2028 dates not yet announced
Metropolitan Expo, Spata; receptions across Piraeus
Berths at Zea and Mikrolimano are scarce that week: confirm early

items.name: The Veakeio summer season
items.teaser: Concerts and theatre under the sky on Profitis Ilias hill, from early June through the summer
items.story: The Veakeio, the municipal open-air theatre on Profitis Ilias hill above Mikrolimano, runs a summer season of concerts, revue and theatre from early June. In 2026 performances were under way by 4 June, when the revue Ego tha sas ta po played at 21:00. The programme is announced in late spring on the theatre's own site, and evening shows start after dark, when the heat has gone off the stone seats.
items.why: Pair a Veakeio night with an early dinner on the Kastella hill.
facts: Early June to late summer; 2027 programme not yet announced
Bring a cushion for the stone seats
